findings.issue: The hero photo (/media/photos/general-hero-1-*.webp) has a banner's lettering baked into it ("Swim for Sunlit Days", "New silhouettes, richer textures and summer-ready prints", "Shop Swimwear" and "Explore the Collection" button outlines), and on desktop our H1, lead and Request a quote button sit right on top of it, so two sets of text overlap and neither reads cleanly (the phone crop happens to hide it).
findings.reference: The competitor's hero photo carries no text of its own; the only words on it are the live eyebrow, H1, lead and buttons, set on a clean darkened left side.
findings.fix: Site Factory replaces the home hero photo (and its 480/960/1536 and phone crops) with a lifestyle shot that has no text, buttons or graphic overlay in it; the overlay CSS stays as it is.

findings.issue: Two trust figures read as broken sentence fragments, "65 that / SAMPLING TEAM" and "55 custom / DAILY SAMPLES", and "100,000 pieces" carries its unit in the value (which wraps it to two lines on phones and pushes its label out of line with "FOUNDED").
findings.reference: The competitor's trust line gives clean figure-and-label pairs ("Since 1993 · 300+ independent labels · custom samples in 1 to 3 weeks").
findings.fix: In src/data/site-trust.json (from Site Factory) set the values to bare figures, e.g. "65" with label "Sampling team", "55" with label "Custom samples a day", "100,000" with label "Pieces a month".

findings.issue: The numbering restarts at 01 in every continuation grid (m2 01–03, m2-2 01–03, m2-3 01–02, and likewise m3/m3-2, featureGrid-4/5/6, featureGrid-7/8, featureGrid-9/10), so one card set reads "01 02 03 01 02 03 01 02" and doesn't come across as one numbered section.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered cards ("01. Custom Designs", "02. Ready Designs", "03. Mix n' Match") count straight through the set.
findings.fix: In the featureGrid component, carry the card counter across grids that "continues" a set (e.g. pass a start index and set counter-reset/the rendered number from it), so m2-2 starts at 04 and m2-3 at 07.

findings.issue: m3 opens its card set with two cards centred under the heading, while its continuation m3-2 directly below sets its two cards from the left column, so the same set's cards stand out of line by about half a card.
findings.reference: The competitor's card row starts on the content's left edge under its heading.
findings.fix: In the featureGrid template CSS, centre a short row only in the set's last grid; a first or middle grid (m3, which has a continuation) starts under the first column like m3-2.

findings.issue: New card sets (featureGrid-1, featureGrid-4, featureGrid-7, featureGrid-9) start directly under the previous set in the same three-up outlined-card shape, so m2 to featureGrid-10 forms one unbroken wall of about seventeen identical card grids (about 5,800 px on desktop, far longer on phones) with no visible boundary between topics.
findings.reference: The competitor uses its outlined numbered cards once ("3 Ways To Get Started") and changes module shape from section to section.
findings.fix: Apply the template's own rule to these sets: where a card set follows another of the same shape, render the second as a list beside its heading (the featureGrid bullets/iconList list layout) instead of another card grid.

findings.issue: The new card sets featureGrid-1, featureGrid-4, featureGrid-7 and featureGrid-9 are all white like the sets before them, so neighbouring plain sections from m2 to featureGrid-10 never alternate white and tint, and featureGrid-1's headingless lead ("You can choose from triangle, bandeau…") sits about 15 px under m2-3's cards as if it belonged to them.
findings.reference: The competitor alternates its plain sections between white, cream and pale blue ("We Build Swimwear Brands" cream, "Digital Patterns" white, "Fabrics in Stock" blue).
findings.fix: Have the template's background alternation count a continuation group (a set and its "continues" grids) as one section, and tint every other group through --section-tint, so featureGrid-1 and featureGrid-7 take the tint.

findings.issue: At 390 px the card title "Quality problem resolution" is hyphenated as "Quality prob- / lem resolution" (template.css:250 sets hyphens: auto on .feature-card__title).
findings.reference: The competitor never hyphenates its headings; long titles wrap at word boundaries.
findings.fix: In template.css change .feature-grid .feature-card .feature-card__title to hyphens: manual (keeping overflow-wrap: break-word only as a last resort for one over-long word).

findings.issue: splitMedia-1 and splitMedia-2 continue m4 ("continues": "m4", variant "tinted") but render on white while m4 is tinted cream, so the Wholesale section breaks into one tinted row and two white ones, and three white sections (splitMedia-1, splitMedia-2, owner-logos) stand in a row.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one section's rows on one background and changes it only between sections.
findings.fix: Have a splitMedia continuation take its parent's background (render splitMedia-1/2 with m4's tinted --section-tint) and start the next background alternation at owner-logos.

findings.issue: The quality-check steps are still a plain browser-numbered list: "1."–"5." markers in body size and colour, and each step's label ("Fabric on arrival") in the same weight as its detail, with the caption "Quality checks at every stage of an order" at body size, so the block reads as unstyled text beside a near-empty left column.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered module sets each step with a bold numeral and a bold, slightly larger title above lighter text ("01. Custom Designs").
findings.fix: In reference.css, scope to .block--process: list-style none on .point-list__items with a counter, a ::before of counter(step, decimal-leading-zero) in var(--accent-text), weight 700, about twice body size; .point-list__title font-weight 700 at var(--size-subheading) with margin-bottom 0.5rem.

findings.issue: The enquiry steps ("Send your enquiry" … "Sample making begins") have the same plain treatment: browser "1."–"4." markers, step titles in the same weight as their lines, and the intro "From your enquiry to your sample" at body size on the tinted band.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered steps carry bold numerals and bold step titles.
findings.fix: The same .block--process rules as overview-steps in reference.css (counter numerals in the accent colour, bold .point-list__title) style this block as well.

findings.issue: On phones about 60 px of empty space separates the one-line intro "Quality checks at every stage of an order" from step 1, much more than the gap between steps, so the intro looks cut off from its list (cta-steps shows the same gap).
findings.reference: The competitor stacks a module's intro and its items with gaps close to the row spacing.
findings.fix: In reference.css, under the single-column breakpoint, reduce the row-gap between the process intro and .point-list__items in .block--process to about 1–1.5rem.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column the email, phone, address, hours and links are centred (reference.css:81 --footer-brand-align: center), but the STRANDMILL mark above them stays on the left edge, so the column looks misaligned (same on phones, where the centred list also sits between a left-aligned mark and left-aligned folds).
findings.reference: The competitor's "Stay connected" column is centred as a whole: heading, icons and links share one axis.
findings.fix: In reference.css either centre the brand mark too (.site-footer__brand-column .site-footer__brand { margin-inline: auto; justify-self: center }) or set --footer-brand-align: start so the whole column starts on its left edge.

findings.issue: On phones the logo row is hard-cut at both edges: a stray ")" glyph on the left and "SOFTME…" / "Swimwear, U…" chopped on the right, which reads as overflow rather than a moving strip.
findings.reference: The competitor's brand row on phones shows whole logos and lets the row run off softly.
findings.fix: In reference.css give the logos marquee track a mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, #000 2rem, #000 calc(100% - 2rem), transparent) so items fade at the edges.

findings.issue: The closing band's "Request a quote" is a thin white outline button on the dark photo, the weakest button on the page at the point it matters most.
findings.reference: The competitor's closing "Launch Your Swimwear Label" band uses solid white pill buttons with dark text.
findings.fix: In reference.css give .block--cta .button on the image band a solid white background with dark text (keeping the pill radius).

findings.issue: The section is titled "Related products and services" but its links are Blog, Case Studies and Privacy Policy, none of them a product or service.
findings.reference: The competitor links onward to its matching service pages ("Explore Sampling", "Explore MOQ & Timelines").
findings.fix: Site Factory points the related links at product or service pages (e.g. Women's Swimwear, Development, Custom Printing) or retitles the block to match the links it keeps.

findings.issue: On phones sections open with only about 24 px above their heading (overview, iconList-1, m2, faq), so headings sit tight under the band or photo before them and the page feels cramped.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves roughly 60–80 px above each section's eyebrow or heading on phones.
findings.fix: In reference.css raise the lower bound of --section-space (clamp(3rem, 6vw, 5.4rem)) to about 4.5rem so small screens get more air between sections.

findings.issue: A 30-word lead ('Since 2011 we have run bulk lines…') sits on the hero photo under the title, because the template's on-photo limit (heroText.leadWords: 27) is measured from the competitor's home hero and applied to every page type; the copy also shows the 'stands under the hero' rule is not kept on phones.
findings.reference: The competitor's About hero is the sewing-floor photo with only the centred white H1 on it: no lead and no button.
findings.fix: Make the on-photo limit per page type (heroText.leadWords, or an equivalent per pageType, 0 for about) so PageHero.astro's heroLeadShown() moves the about lead under the hero.

findings.issue: Two of the four figures are cut phrases, '65 that' over 'SAMPLING TEAM' and '55 custom' over 'DAILY SAMPLES', so the bar reads as broken copy at both widths.
findings.reference: The competitor's figure bars set a short value phrase ('2-3 days') over a clear uppercase label.
findings.fix: Site Factory: rewrite the value/label pairs, e.g. '65' / 'person sampling team' and '55' / 'custom samples a day'.

findings.issue: The check-list item headings ('Checks throughout production', 'Experienced inspection team') are in regular weight at almost the section heading's size and wrap into two loosely spaced lines, so they read like enlarged body text rather than a level under the h2 (same at desktop).
findings.reference: The competitor sets its sub-headings in Maison 700 (h3 26px), and our own featureGrid card titles on this page are bold.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `.icon-list__item h3 { font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; }`; leave the size to the template.

findings.issue: Same as m5: the item headings 'Certifications held', 'Production audit requirements' and 'Market compliance paperwork' are regular-weight, almost h2-sized and loosely wrapped, so they don't stand apart from the body text.
findings.reference: The competitor's sub-headings are Maison 700.
findings.fix: The same `.icon-list__item h3 { font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; }` rule in reference.css covers this block.

findings.issue: The 'STRANDMILL' wordmark sits on the left edge while the email, phone, address, hours and links under it are centred, so the brand column is split in two alignments.
findings.reference: The competitor's footer brand column (monogram, STAY CONNECTED, links) is centred as one on both phone and desktop.
findings.fix: template.css:297 `.site-footer__brand { justify-self: start }` overrides the column's --footer-brand-align (patterns.css:43); make the brand follow the column, e.g. `justify-self: var(--footer-brand-justify, start)`, set from --footer-brand-align.

findings.issue: On desktop too, the wordmark starts at the column's left edge while the contact lines and page links under it are centred.
findings.reference: The competitor's desktop brand column is centred top to bottom.
findings.fix: The same template.css justify-self fix on `.site-footer__brand`.

findings.issue: The six steps wrap into two rows of three, but the connecting line only runs through the first row (and on past marker 03 to the edge), so steps 04–06 look detached from the sequence.
findings.reference: The competitor's six-step module sets every step over the same hairline.
findings.fix: Draw the process rule per row (e.g. on each step's marker row instead of a single `.process-steps::before`), ending at the row's last marker.

findings.issue: The step titles ('Final sample approval', 'Order confirmation') are regular weight at almost body size, so each step's title barely separates from its text (same at desktop).
findings.reference: The competitor's step and card titles are bold (Maison 700).
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `.block--process .process-step__title { font-weight: 700; }`.

findings.issue: '100,000 pieces' wraps to two lines while '2011' beside it takes one, so 'MONTHLY CAPACITY' sits about 24px below 'FOUNDED' in the same row.
findings.reference: The competitor's figure columns keep value and label level across a row.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `.trust-bar__value { white-space: nowrap; }` (the value fits the 175px column), or bottom-align the labels in the row.

findings.issue: The moving logo row is clipped with a hard edge at the content gutters, cutting wordmarks mid-letter ('HFOLD SICS' at the left, 'S' at the right).
findings.reference: The competitor's logo marquee runs across the full width with no visible cut-off.
findings.fix: Let the logos-marquee rail bleed to the viewport edges, or fade its ends with `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, #000 2rem, #000 calc(100% - 2rem), transparent)`.

findings.issue: The check marks are small, pale aqua on white (well under 3:1) and sit above the first line of their item heading instead of level with it.
findings.reference: The competitor's check lists use clearly visible marks set level with the item text.
findings.fix: In reference.css, colour the icon-list check with the darker accent text colour (--accent-text) and align it to the heading's first line (align-self/margin-top on the icon).

findings.issue: The steps companion renders as a bare ordered list: plain '1.'–'6.' numerals, each step title ('Brief or tech pack') set smaller than and no bolder than its own description, under a body-size caption ('How a typical order runs') floating alone in an otherwise empty left half, so the steps read as unstyled text.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered-steps module (solution page, process:list) sets each step with a blue 01–03 numeral and a heading-weight title above its text.
findings.fix: In the shared steps component (.prose__steps), give the item title the subheading size/weight above its description (never below it) and style the marker as the accent numeral used by process steps; keep the list-beside-caption arrangement.

findings.issue: Same bare-list rendering as overview-steps: 'Sign off sample and specs' and the other step titles are smaller than their descriptions and the same weight, with plain '1.'–'4.' numerals under a body-size caption.
findings.reference: The competitor numbers steps 01–03 in blue with a heading-weight title above the text.
findings.fix: Same component fix as overview-steps (.prose__steps item title hierarchy and accent numerals).

findings.issue: On phones the caption 'How a typical order runs' is followed by an empty band of about 50px before the list starts (m8-steps shows the same gap), so the caption reads as detached from its steps.
findings.reference: The competitor's step lists follow their heading at the normal heading-to-content gap.
findings.fix: In the stacked (single-column) layout of .prose__steps, drop the side-by-side row gap and use the heading-to-content gap between caption and list.

findings.issue: Each step's title ('Agree commercial details', 'Confirm production details'…) is set at the same 17px regular weight as the description under it, so the titles do not stand out from the text. Desktop shows the same at its smaller size.
findings.reference: The competitor's step and card titles are set in its bold weight (Maison 700) above regular body text.
findings.fix: Set font-weight: 700 (var(--font-ui)) on .block--process .process-step title in reference.css; leave its size to the template.

findings.issue: Two check lists of the same shape stand one under the other: m3 'Stock Styles & Wholesale Buying' and m6 'Pricing & Quotes' both set their items as a list beside their heading, so the page shows the same arrangement twice in a row.
findings.reference: Site rule: of two neighbouring sections of rows of short items, the template sets only one as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: Have the template give m6 (or m3) the other iconList arrangement (items under the heading in columns) when two iconList sections are neighbours.

findings.issue: The check marks before each list item are a pale aqua on the beige tint (and on white in m6/m7/m9), at roughly 1.5:1 contrast, so they barely show at either width.
findings.reference: The competitor's check list and icons use its navy/steel blue on light grounds; non-text graphics need 3:1.
findings.fix: Set the iconList checks variant marker colour (the icon's color/stroke in .block--iconList) to the dark accent (#1f5a7a / #306180) in reference.css.

findings.issue: The list item titles ('Individual style pricing', 'Construction and materials'…) are set in a light regular weight at nearly the section heading's size, so they read as loose large text, not titles, unlike the bold card titles in m2 directly above.
findings.reference: The competitor's item and card titles are Maison 700, the same weight as its headings.
findings.fix: Set font-weight: 700 on the iconList item title in reference.css (all iconList blocks), matching .featureGrid card titles; the size stays the template's.

findings.issue: This block has no heading and continues m11, but its first paragraph ('We measure your packed cartons…') takes the larger lead size, while proof-5 and proof-6 just before it do not. One paragraph in the middle of the section grows for no reason (also on mobile).
findings.reference: The competitor's text sections keep one body size through their paragraphs (Maison Book 17px/25.5px).
findings.fix: Apply the lead style only to the first paragraph under a section heading, never to the first paragraph of a headless continuation block.

findings.issue: The fee chart draws three identical full-width bars for Sample fee, Design fee and Courier delivery (all $50), which compares nothing. The timing chart's two range bars float on tracks with no axis or scale.
findings.reference: The competitor shows figures only where they add information (a fabric chart figure, stats tiles with big numbers and captions).
findings.fix: Have Site Factory give these figures as a stats row or short list (three $50 fees; 10–15 and 5–7 days) rather than bar charts of equal values.

findings.issue: The single related link 'Case Studies' is drawn as one outlined bar across the full ~1400px container, with its label at the far left and its arrow at the far right, so it looks like an empty input field.
findings.reference: The competitor's link rows (contact channel rows, toggle rows) are sized to a column, not stretched across the page.
findings.fix: Cap the width of the relatedPages links list in reference.css (e.g. grid with repeat(auto-fill, minmax(18rem, 1fr)) or a max-width on .related items) so a lone link stays at one column.

findings.issue: The heading 'Related products and services' sits over a single link to 'Case Studies', which is neither a product nor a service.
findings.reference: n/a (copy).
findings.fix: Have Site Factory either link related product/solution pages here or retitle the section to match its link.

findings.issue: In the brand column the STRANDMILL wordmark is left-aligned while the email, phone, address, hours and links under it are centred, so the column has two alignments. Mobile shows the same.
findings.reference: The competitor's footer brand column (monogram, STAY CONNECTED, icons, links) is centred as a whole, on desktop and on phones.
findings.fix: Add text-align: center (or align-self: center) to .site-footer__brand in reference.css so the wordmark follows --footer-brand-align: center.

findings.issue: The thin rule meant to separate the brand column from the link columns does not show: it is drawn in rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3) on the #003049 navy.
findings.reference: The competitor separates its brand column from the four link columns with a visible thin vertical rule.
findings.fix: Change the border-right colour on .site-footer__brand-column (reference.css, min-width 1024px) to a light rule such as rgb(255 255 255 / 0.3).

findings.issue: The two order-case cards sit in a narrow centred column (about 920–1288 px of the 1440 frame) while the heading 'A recent order' starts on the content's left edge, which leaves roughly 330 px of empty tint to the left of the cards and as much to the right, so the cards float mid-page instead of following their heading.
findings.reference: The competitor's card sets start on the content's left edge under their heading and fill the content width, e.g. home section 7's outlined cards in a row.
findings.fix: In patterns.css, `.order-cases { max-width: 46rem; margin-inline: auto; }` should not centre when headings start: under `body[data-heading-align="start"]` set `.order-cases { margin-inline: 0; }` (or lay two or three cases side by side in a grid of equal columns from the left edge).

findings.issue: The six steps look like a plain ordered list: small default numerals, step titles ('Brief or tech pack', 'Sample' …) in the same size and weight as their details, and the caption 'How a typical order moves through our factory' at body size alone in the left column over about 360 px of empty space.
findings.reference: The competitor sets steps out as a module: six columns, each with a number, a bold title and text over a hairline (start-here section 6, process:timeline), or numbered steps with blue numerals beside a left heading (process:list).
findings.fix: In template-variants.json give the general page type a process variant (`pageTypes.general.process: "timeline"`, matching the competitor's six-step columns); in reference.css set the step title of `.block--process` to font-weight 700 so it stands apart from its detail.

findings.issue: The four takeover steps have the same plain-list treatment: default numerals, titles at the weight of their text, and the caption at body size alone in the left column over an empty column.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered steps: number, bold title and text over a hairline (process:timeline / process:list).
findings.fix: Covered by the same change as overview-steps: a process variant for the general page type in template-variants.json (`timeline`), and a 700 weight for the step title of `.block--process` in reference.css.

findings.issue: 'Frequently Asked Questions' breaks into three one-word lines in the narrow left column of the two-column FAQ, so the heading looks stacked rather than sized to its words.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ (home 16) sets the 52px h2 across the width on one line, with the questions in columns below it.
findings.fix: In the faq two-column layout, widen the heading column, or set the heading above the questions when the template's fit would break it into one word per line.

findings.issue: Each order-case card carries a thick 3px aqua rule down its left edge, curved by the card radius, which the competitor's cards never use.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards are outlined in 1px (black or #979797) with 6–10px corners, no accent rule and no shadow.
findings.fix: In reference.css override `.order-case` to `border: 1px solid #979797; border-left-width: 1px;` (keeping its radius) in place of the 3px accent left border.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column the STRANDMILL wordmark is set left, while the email, phone, address, hours and page links under it are centred, so the column has two alignments.
findings.reference: The competitor's footer brand column centres its logo, 'STAY CONNECTED', icons and links on one axis.
findings.fix: In reference.css centre `.site-footer__brand` (text-align / justify-self from `--footer-brand-align: center`) to match the centred lines under it.

findings.issue: On phones the STRANDMILL wordmark starts on the left edge while every contact line and page link under it is centred.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone footer centres its logo, 'STAY CONNECTED' and links.
findings.fix: Same change as on desktop: centre `.site-footer__brand` in reference.css, following `--footer-brand-align: center`.

findings.issue: The proof section has no top padding: its opening line ('Orders start at 50 pieces…') starts on the section's top edge, right under m2's last item, so the label covers it and the two sections run together; proof-2 does the same under the chart.
findings.reference: The competitor's text sections keep a clear gap above their first line, as wide as the gap between its other sections.
findings.fix: Keep the .block padding-block (calc(var(--section-space) / 2)) at the top of .block--proof[data-variant="band"] when it follows a section with the same background, instead of dropping it to 0; same for proof-2 under proof-1-charts.

findings.issue: On phones proof-1 and proof-2 also start flush with their top edge, so their first line touches the previous section's last item ('…within one business day.' / the chart card) with no gap.
findings.reference: The competitor's mobile text blocks have the same top gap as every other section.
findings.fix: Same fix as on desktop: give .block--proof its normal top padding when it follows a same-background neighbour.

findings.issue: The alternating backgrounds stop after m3: m2, proof-1, proof-1-charts (white, with only an inset tinted card) and proof-2 are all white in a row, at both widths, so the white/tint rhythm breaks for four sections.
findings.reference: The competitor separates neighbouring sections by background.
findings.fix: Have the template's alternation count the proof/charts group as one plain section and tint it (through --section-tint), so m2 (white), proof group (tint), process-1 (white) alternate.

findings.issue: The order-path process looks unstyled: its title 'From your brief to shipment: the typical order path' is set at body size and weight rather than as a heading, and its steps are a plain browser-numbered list (1., 2.) with step names in the same weight as their descriptions, unlike the circle-marker steps of process-1 just above.
findings.reference: The competitor's steps modules set a section heading over numbered markers, with each step name in a heavier subheading weight.
findings.fix: Render the process list variant's title as the section h2 (template heading fit), and give its steps the same marker and name treatment (.process-step marker plus a 600-weight name) as the circles variant; or set cta-steps to the circles variant used by process-1.

findings.issue: On phones the order path reads as body copy: a small paragraph, a large empty gap, then a default numbered list whose numbers hang outside the text edge and whose step names are no heavier than their lines.
findings.reference: The competitor's mobile steps stack under a heading, each with a marker and a bold step name.
findings.fix: Same as desktop: an h2 for the title, the circles marker and 600-weight step names, and the list's numbers aligned to the content edge (list-style none with the template marker).

findings.issue: Two iconList sections of the same shape (heading on the left, column of check-marked short items on the right) stand one under the other (m3, then m2), so the page repeats one layout twice in a row.
findings.reference: The competitor doesn't repeat a module back to back; the site's rule sets one of two same-shaped sections out differently.
findings.fix: Let the template set one of two consecutive iconList sections in another arrangement (e.g. m2 as a two-column item grid under its heading) when they stand next to each other.

findings.issue: The check-list item titles are regular weight, about 26px, with a loose line height, so two-line titles ('Shipping costs / remain payable', 'Written return / authorization') come apart and come close in size to the section heading.
findings.reference: The competitor's item subheadings are set tight and in a heavier weight, clearly below the section heading.
findings.fix: In reference.css set the iconList item title (.icon-list__item h3) line-height to about 1.25 and font-weight to 500–600; applies to m2 too.

findings.issue: The single related link ('Privacy Policy') stretches across the whole content width in a thin bordered box with an arrow at the far end, so it looks like an empty form input rather than a link card.
findings.reference: The competitor's link cards are sized to their content and laid out in a row of card widths.
findings.fix: Cap the related link card at one card width (max-width of a grid column, e.g. the template's card track) rather than 100%, keeping it on the content's left edge.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column the STRANDMILL wordmark sits on the left edge while the contact lines and links under it are centred, so the column has two alignments (same on desktop).
findings.reference: The competitor centres its footer logo and 'STAY CONNECTED' over the centred contact links.
findings.fix: Apply --footer-brand-align: center to .site-footer__brand too (text-align/justify-self: var(--footer-brand-align)) so the wordmark is centred over its column.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column the STRANDMILL name sits on the column's left edge while the email, phone, address, hours and page links under it are centred, so the column reads as two alignments.
findings.reference: The competitor centres its whole brand column as one: logo, STAY CONNECTED, social icons and links all on the column's centre line.
findings.fix: In template.css (line 297), change `.site-footer__brand { justify-self: start }` to `justify-self: var(--footer-brand-align, start)` (or stretch it), so the name follows `.site-footer__brand-column { text-align: var(--footer-brand-align) }` like its contact lines and links; this site sets --footer-brand-align: center.

findings.issue: On phones the STRANDMILL name is left-aligned above a stack of centred contact lines and links, so the name looks unattached to the block it heads.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone footer centres the logo, STAY CONNECTED and its links together above the folded groups.
findings.fix: Same fix as on desktop: let `.site-footer__brand` follow --footer-brand-align instead of `justify-self: start` in template.css.

findings.issue: The thin rule meant to separate the brand column from the link columns can't be seen: it is drawn in black at 30% on the dark navy footer.
findings.reference: The competitor's footer shows a faint light vertical rule between the brand column and the link columns.
findings.fix: In reference.css, change `.site-footer__brand-column { border-right: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3) }` (≥1024px) to a light rule such as `rgb(255 255 255 / 0.15)`.

findings.issue: The only related link (Terms and Conditions) is one outlined bar that runs the full ~1400px content width, with a small label at the far left and its arrow at the far right, so it looks like an empty form field rather than a link.
findings.reference: The competitor's about page has no matching module; it links onward with short inline text links that stay their own length.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set the relatedPages list to a grid of capped tracks (e.g. `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(18rem, 24rem))`) so a lone item takes one card's width instead of stretching across the row.

findings.issue: The heading 'Related products and services' sits over a single link to Terms and Conditions, which is neither a product nor a service.
findings.reference: The competitor's onward links say where they lead (e.g. 'Read the full group story … at PT King Trading').
findings.fix: Site Factory: retitle the section to fit its link (e.g. 'Related policies'), or link the products and services pages the heading names.

findings.issue: The tinted related band has about 25px of top and bottom padding, half the gap of the intro section above it (~50px), so its heading sits close to the band's top edge.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one even vertical gap between its content sections.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give the relatedPages section the same block padding as the other plain sections (the template's section padding, not a reduced one).

findings.issue: At 390 px the table keeps two columns, so the answer column is about 180 px wide and each cell runs 8 to 16 short lines. The section ends up about 2,970 px tall, mostly a narrow ragged strip with the Topic column almost empty beside it.
findings.reference: The competitor's long text runs in full-width blocks on phones, with comfortable line lengths and no narrow side columns.
findings.fix: Set components.pageTypes.blog_hub.blocks.table-1.variant to "cards" in template-variants.json. Each row then reads as its topic over its full-width answer on phones; the desktop rows keep their rules.

findings.issue: The hero is a plain text header on white, with no photo. Its title and lead sit straight on top of the next section, so the page opens without the photo band the competitor's matching page starts with.
findings.reference: The competitor's page (the about page this one is matched to) opens on a full-width workshop photo under an even dark overlay, with its bold white title over it.
findings.fix: Set components.blog.hub.header to "banner" in template-variants.json, the existing photo backdrop with a 0.5 overlay. That puts the title on a photo band as the competitor does, and the long lead stays under it as today's lead does.

findings.issue: The H1 "The Strandmill Blog" is set in DM Sans 400 while every H2 below it is 700. The page title looks thinner and weaker than the section headings under it, so the order of the headings reads backwards.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its page title ("About Swimwear Bali") in a bold weight, heavier than its body text and at least as heavy as its section headings.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give `.blog-hub-hero h1` font-weight: 700 (or 600). Change the weight only; leave the fitted font-size as it is.

findings.issue: The quality steps still use the browser's default "1." to "5." markers at body size and colour. The step names ("Fabric on arrival", "Cutting" and so on) have the same weight as their descriptions, so the section reads as a plain ordered list rather than a process. This was already raised on the style board (board--process-list) and is still unfixed on this page.
findings.reference: The competitor's process list marks each step with a large, accent-blue, zero-padded numeral (01, 02, 03) in its own column. Each step's name is bold above its text, and thin light rules divide the steps.
findings.fix: In reference.css, scoped to .block--process, set .point-list__items to list-style: none with a decimal-leading-zero counter. Draw it in an accent-coloured, weight-700 ::before column, give .point-list__title font-weight: 700, and add border-top: 1px solid var(--border-color) to each .point-list__item.

findings.issue: The section has no heading. Its only intro is the body-size caption "Quality checks at every stage of an order.", so the left column is a single small line beside a long list, between two bold H2 sections.
findings.reference: The competitor's process list always opens with an H2 above its lead, in the left column beside the steps.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give the overview-quality-stages visual (blog.json) a heading, for example "Quality Checks at Every Stage", so the block renders an H2 above the caption.

findings.issue: Four plain sections in a row (hero, overview, overview-steps, table-1) all have white backgrounds. Nothing separates them except the section padding, and the hero's lead runs straight into the overview heading.
findings.reference: The site's rule, which follows the competitor's banded pages, is that neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds.
findings.fix: The template should alternate the plain sections' backgrounds (white, then var(--section-tint) from the treatment's --surface-secondary #f4eee6). Here that would give overview-steps a tint between the white overview and table-1.

findings.issue: On phones a band of about 60 to 70 px separates the one-line caption from the first step. That is much more than the gap between steps, so the caption looks cut off from its list.
findings.reference: The competitor stacks a process module's intro and steps with gaps close to its row spacing.
findings.fix: In reference.css, below the stacking breakpoint, cut the row-gap between the intro column and .point-list__items in .block--process to the list's own gap (about 1 to 1.5rem).

findings.issue: At 1440 px the answer cells run across the whole container, so lines are about 140 to 150 characters long (for example the Certifications and Fabrics rows). That is well beyond a readable measure.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps its running text to roughly 65 to 85 characters a line.
findings.fix: In reference.css, cap the answer cells at the text measure, for example `.table-block td:last-child { max-width: 75ch; }`. Leave the table's own width free.

findings.issue: The "STRANDMILL" wordmark is aligned left while everything listed under it (the email, phone, address, hours and links) is centred. The column has two alignments, at 390 px and in the first column at 1440 px.
findings.reference: The competitor centres its whole brand column: the logo, "STAY CONNECTED", the contact links and the social icons share one centre line.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .site-footer__brand text-align: center (justify-self: center) so it shares the brand column's centre, or set that column's contact lines to start-aligned to match the wordmark.

findings.issue: The four channel cards are held at a fixed width (--channel-card-width: 15.3125rem, copied from the competitor), so the row is centred and takes up only about the middle 70% of the content width. It doesn't start under the left-aligned 'Contact details' heading, and the Hours card breaks its time after the hyphen ('9:00-' / '18:00 China Standard Time').
findings.reference: The competitor's four cards fill the width of their own content column, level with the form and photo above them. Only their style is to be followed (1px #979797 border, radius 10px, icon, black label bar, centred text), not their pixel width.
findings.fix: In reference.css remove --channel-card-width so the cards share the content width and the row starts on the content's left edge under the heading. Keep '9:00–18:00' on one line (white-space: nowrap on the time, or a non-breaking dash in the copy).

findings.issue: The 'Contact details' heading sits right on the first card's top border with almost no gap. At desktop the gap is only a few pixels. Every other section on the page leaves clear space between its heading and its content.
findings.reference: The competitor's card row is set well apart from the content above it, and its headings ('Have Questions?', 'Email Us') have clear space under them.
findings.fix: In reference.css give the channels heading the same space below it as the other sections (e.g. margin-block-end on .block--contactChannels .block__heading, or a row-gap between the heading and .contact-channels).

findings.issue: The five steps show as a plain numbered browser list. The step titles ('Send your files', 'We check feasibility') have the same weight and size as their descriptions, the text is smaller than the intro's body copy, and the lead ('How a free quote moves…') looks like a loose body line. Nothing marks this as a process module.
findings.reference: The competitor's process list (solution page, process:list) is a left heading and text with numbered steps on the right: large blue numerals 01–03, a bold title per step, then text.
findings.fix: Set components.pageTypes.contact.process to "list" in template-variants.json so the steps get numbered markers and bold step titles at body size.

findings.issue: The steps are unstyled here too (plain '1.'–'5.' with titles at body weight). There is also a gap of about 60 px with nothing in it between the lead line and the first step.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered steps stack straight under their heading and text, each with a numeral and a bold title.
findings.fix: This is fixed by the same process variant ('list'). Then check that the gap between the lead and the steps matches the other sections' heading-to-content gap.

findings.issue: The list item titles ('Contact channels', 'Dedicated specialist', …) are set in regular (400) weight at about 26 px. That is almost the size of the section's 700-weight H2 just above them, so the levels blur and the list reads like a run of headings. The light-teal check marks are also so faint they nearly disappear on the tint.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each level smaller than the one above and its item titles bold (card titles Maison 700 22px under 52–60px h2s). Its check lists use clearly visible markers.
findings.fix: Set components.pageTypes.contact.iconList to "checks", or in reference.css give .block--iconList item titles font-weight 700 and the subheading scale under the h2. Give the check icon a darker colour (e.g. var(--surface-dark) or the link blue).

findings.issue: At desktop too, the item titles are a light 400 weight at a size close to the body lead, with a pale check icon. Next to the bold 700 H2 they look unfinished.
findings.reference: The competitor's item titles are bold (Maison 700) and its markers are clearly visible.
findings.fix: Same change as on mobile: the 'checks' variant, or font-weight 700 on the item titles and a darker check colour.

findings.issue: The consent checkbox is a tiny, pale square of about 12 px, barely visible on the tint and well below a comfortable tap size. It is the one required tick in the form.
findings.reference: The competitor's form fields all have clear 1px black outlines and full-size tap targets.
findings.fix: In reference.css give the form's checkbox a visible 1px black border (or accent-color: #262626) and a size of about 20–24 px, with the label wrapping beside it.

findings.issue: 'SEND ENQUIRY' is a small dark button at the left of the form column. The comment in reference.css calls for a full-width dark SEND bar, but the rule never sets the width.
findings.reference: The competitor's submit is a full-width dark bar (#262626) across the form column.
findings.fix: Add width: 100% (or justify-self: stretch) to the :is(.form-block__form, .cta__form) .button--primary rule in reference.css.

findings.issue: The consent line ends 'as described in the privacy policy. Privacy policy': the words 'privacy policy' appear twice because the copy repeats the link label that follows it.
findings.reference: The competitor's form has no repeated text.
findings.fix: Shorten the consent copy to end before the link (e.g. 'I agree that my details are used to answer this enquiry, as described in our') or make 'privacy policy' in the sentence itself the link.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column, the STRANDMILL wordmark sits on the left edge while the contact lines and links beneath it are centred, so the column has two alignments.
findings.reference: The competitor's brand column is centred throughout: monogram, STAY CONNECTED, the social icons and the links.
findings.fix: In template.css let .site-footer__brand follow the column (justify-self/text-align: var(--footer-brand-align, start)) instead of a fixed justify-self: start. This site already sets --footer-brand-align: center.

findings.issue: On phones the STRANDMILL wordmark is also left-aligned above a centred block of contact lines and links.
findings.reference: On phones the competitor centres everything in the footer.
findings.fix: Same template change: .site-footer__brand takes var(--footer-brand-align).

findings.issue: The check-list item titles ('Standalone orders', 'Focused first range' …) are set in a light 400 weight, so under the 500-weight section heading they read as large body text rather than sub-headings; the same treatment runs through iconList-2, m3 and m10 at both widths.
findings.reference: The competitor sets every sub-heading under a section heading bold ('Pricing Custom Swimwear Designs', 'Ready Designs', 'Custom Designs' in its MOQs block).
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give the iconList item title (h3) font-weight: 600–700 and line-height ~1.25, leaving its size to the template.

findings.issue: On phones the check-list item titles ('Exposure and finish', 'Custom mould fee', 'Hardware ordering' …) are fitted to about 26px, almost the size of the section heading 'Custom Metal Hardware, Charms and Finishes' above them, so the two heading levels look the same (also in iconList-1, iconList-2 and m10).
findings.reference: The competitor keeps each heading level clearly smaller than the one above (its bold sub-heads sit just above body size under a larger h2).
findings.fix: In the shared heading-fit step, cap an item (h3) heading's fitted size below its section h2's size (e.g. at most ~0.75 of the h2), so a short item title can no longer grow to the h2's size on phones.

findings.issue: Each point's title ('Production standards', 'Direct factory control', 'In-house development', 'Contact our team') is in regular weight and smaller than the paragraph under it, with plain black disc bullets, so the list reads as one run of text with the hierarchy inverted; m9 has the same treatment at both widths.
findings.reference: The competitor's sub-heads are bold and at or above body size ('Pricing Custom Swimwear Designs', 'Ready Designs'), so each item can be scanned on its own.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set .point-list__title to the heading face at weight 700 with a font-size at least equal to the item text, and restyle the [data-pattern="bullets"] markers with the accent check (as iconList uses) instead of the default disc.

findings.issue: The step titles ('Brief and fees', 'Sample review', 'Bulk production', 'Final inspection') are the same size and weight as the step text under them, so the four steps have no visible heading over their details (same on mobile).
findings.reference: The competitor's sub-heads over a block of text are bold ('Pricing Custom Swimwear Designs', 'Ready Designs').
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set the .block--process step title to font-weight 700 (leaving its size to the template).

findings.issue: The check marks are thin pale-aqua strokes that nearly vanish on the beige tint (and on white in iconList-2, m3 and m10), so the list's marker barely registers.
findings.reference: The competitor uses its deep blue for accents on light grounds (its links #1670a8) and keeps pale aqua for filled shapes, not thin strokes.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css colour the iconList check icon with the darker accent (var(--accent-text) / #1670a8) or thicken its stroke to reach 3:1 against both white and the tint.

findings.issue: The cost chart draws a full black grid around every cell (the m5 strap table does too), while the m6 table on the same page uses only light row rules, so the page has two table styles and the boxed one looks heavy.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its tabular facts (the MOQs block, the costing handover) without boxed cell grids; its rules are single hairlines.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give the charts and splitMedia panel tables the m6 table's treatment: no vertical cell borders and row rules in a light colour (e.g. color-mix of --text-primary at ~18%) instead of --border-color #000.

findings.issue: The 'Specification and use' column spans about 1,100px, so its cells run single lines of 150–180 characters ('Transparent elastic tape stops slipping inside waistbands, chest lines and leg openings…'), far past a readable measure.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps its body copy to lines of about 75–90 characters (its centred text column is about 930px at a 15px size).
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css cap the table's width (e.g. .block--table table { max-inline-size: 70rem; }) or the cell text (td { max-inline-size: 75ch; }) so its lines stay near 75–90 characters.

findings.issue: The three quote cards stop about 100px short of the content's right edge, which every other section (the related links below, the cards above) reaches, so the row looks cut short.
findings.reference: The competitor's card rows run the full content width with even gutters (its three outlined cards in a row).
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css let the testimonials grid columns stretch to the content width (grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) / no max card width) on desktop.

findings.issue: Card titles that wrap ('Additional / personalisation', and 'Composting / and recycling' in m8-2) use a line spacing of about 1.6, so their two lines drift apart and read as separate lines.
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles are set tight (Maison 700 22px/33px ≈ 1.5 at most, its multi-line headings at ~1.4 or less).
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set the feature-card title (.feature-card__title) line-height to about 1.25.

findings.issue: In the two-by-two trust bar the first value breaks as '2 to 3 working / days', leaving 'days' alone on a centred second line while the other three values keep to one line.
findings.reference: The competitor's short figures stay on one line each.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css let the trust-bar value balance its lines (text-wrap: balance) or keep a figure and its unit together (white-space: nowrap on the value with a slightly smaller value size on phones).

findings.issue: The hero button 'Request a quote for swimwear accessories' wraps to two lines on a full-width black bar (the same button closes the cta block), which looks clumsy for a single action.
findings.reference: The competitor's buttons carry two- or three-word labels ('Request Price', 'Book a Call') that sit on one line on phones.
findings.fix: Shorten the button label in the page copy (e.g. 'Request a quote') so it keeps to one line at 390px.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column the STRANDMILL wordmark is set left while the email, phone, address, hours and page links under it are centred, so the column has two alignments.
findings.reference: The competitor's footer brand column centres 'STAY CONNECTED', its icons and links on one axis.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css centre .site-footer__brand (text-align / justify-self) to match the centred lines under it.

findings.issue: On phones the STRANDMILL wordmark starts on the left edge while every contact line and page link under it is centred.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone footer centres 'STAY CONNECTED' and its links.
findings.fix: Same change as on desktop: centre .site-footer__brand in src/styles/reference.css.

findings.issue: The desktop hero photo has its own headline ('Swim for Sunlit Days'), lead and two buttons printed into the picture; they compete with the real H1 below it, and the frame's bottom edge cuts the second printed button in half.
findings.reference: The competitor's hero is a clean photo with no text on it; the H1, lead and two black buttons stand under the photo.
findings.fix: Replace the hero photo with one that carries no text or buttons (Site Factory photo choice); keep the H1 and button under the photo as they are.

findings.issue: splitMedia-1, splitMedia-2 and its steps block splitMedia-2-steps all have the same beige tint, so tinted sections run one under the other instead of alternating white and tinted (the same on mobile).
findings.reference: The competitor alternates white sections with its pink-tinted Sampling panel; no two tinted modules touch.
findings.fix: The template's background alternation should count splitMedia-1 and splitMedia-2 as neighbouring plain sections and set splitMedia-2 (with its steps) on white, so the tint goes white / tint / white.

findings.issue: Each step's title ('Brief or tech pack', 'Quote and price agreed' …) has the same weight and size as its description, so the seven steps read as fourteen equal lines (the same on desktop).
findings.reference: The competitor sets each item's short title in bold above its regular-weight description (MOQs: 'Custom Designs' / 'Ready Designs').
findings.fix: In reference.css, give the process list's step title (.process-step__title or the list item's title element) font-weight 600 so it stands apart from its description.

findings.issue: The section heading 'How a typical order runs from brief to shipment.' is set at about the step text's size and in regular weight, so it reads as a caption rather than a heading next to the list.
findings.reference: The competitor's section headings ('MOQs', 'Sampling') are clearly bigger than the body text, in a medium weight.
findings.fix: The template should fit this heading to its own words at section-heading level like the page's other H2s (it is now smaller than they are); no font-size set in reference.css.

findings.issue: In the brand column, the STRANDMILL name sits on the column's left edge while the email, phone, address, hours and links under it are centred (the same on mobile).
findings.reference: The competitor centres its whole 'Stay connected' column: title, icons and links on one axis.
findings.fix: In template.css, remove `justify-self: start` (and `align-self: start`) from .site-footer__brand, or make it `justify-self: stretch`, so the name follows .site-footer__brand-column's text-align (--footer-brand-align).

findings.issue: The three testimonial cards fill only the first three columns of a four-column grid, leaving an empty column on the right of the band.
findings.reference: The competitor fills the content width with each row of its modules; there is no empty column at the end.
findings.fix: Lay out the testimonials grid from its card count (three equal columns, or auto-fit instead of auto-fill) so three cards span the content width.

findings.issue: The white 'Sample fee / Design fee' chart card is stretched well below its content, leaving an empty white band of about a third of its height above the payment-terms card.
findings.reference: The competitor's media column holds its picture at its own height with no empty frame.
findings.fix: Let the chart cards in the split's media column take their content height (align-content/align-self: start on the chart set) instead of stretching to a shared row height.

findings.issue: In the 2×2 trust bar, '80/20 nylon-spandex' breaks over two lines while '50 pieces' takes one, so the two labels in the first row ('CORE FABRIC BLEND', 'MINIMUM PER STYLE') sit at different heights.
findings.reference: The competitor's short fact rows keep each row's parts level.
findings.fix: Align the trust-bar items' labels on a shared line (the items as a subgrid, or align-content: end on .stats__item) so each row's labels line up.

findings.issue: The intro paragraphs run about 800px wide, roughly 95–100 characters a line, well past the ~70ch measure (the cta copy is just as wide).
findings.reference: treatment-practice.md holds running text to about 70ch.
findings.fix: Give the intro's (and cta's) text column a max-width of about 70ch in reference.css, starting on the heading's left edge.

findings.issue: The seven related-page tiles run 4 + 3, and the short last row of three starts on the left instead of being centred under the full row.
findings.reference: Site rule: only a grid's own short last row is centred; the competitor has no left-hanging short rows.
findings.fix: Centre the related grid's short last row in the template, as it does for other card grids.

findings.issue: On phones the three-column comparison table is wider than its panel: the right column is cut at the panel edge ('Organizationa…'), a white fade lies over the cells, and the rest squeezes to one or two words per line (the same table treatment cramps splitMedia-1 and splitMedia-3).
findings.reference: The competitor's page uses no tables; at 390 px its two-column comparisons ('Planning your collection' / 'What sells') stack as full-width panels with normal line lengths.
findings.fix: On narrow screens show the comparison table as stacked rows (each row label as a small heading over its two values) instead of a sideways-scrolling grid with an edge fade.

findings.issue: On phones the list-item titles are fitted to about 26 px, larger than the section's h2 (about 24 px); several then break onto a second line with a wide line gap ('Market-specific / compliance', 'Recycled- / content evidence'), so they do not keep to their lines (also in m3, iconList-2 and iconList-3).
findings.reference: The competitor's item titles (the six steps, the 01–03 steps) are a clearly smaller level than the section h2: bold, about 18–20 px on phones, on one line.
findings.fix: Cap the fitted size of an item title under its section heading's size (one level below the h2), and use the heading line-height when it wraps.

findings.issue: On phones the card titles ('Market size and segments', 'Wholesale calendar first') are fitted to the same size as the section h2 above them, and short titles break onto two lines with a large gap ('Positioning / grounded in gaps', 'Unit economics / and capital', 'Fixed-scope / launch projects'); this repeats in m2-2, m4, m5, m7 and m7-2.
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles are one level below the h2 (Maison 700 about 22 px against an h2 of 32 px or more), set solid on one or two lines.
findings.fix: Let the heading fit size a card h3 only up to a step below its section's h2, with heading line-height on the wrap.

findings.issue: The process steps are a plain ordered list: '1. Agree the engagement' has the same size and weight as its description (smaller than it on phones), with browser '1.' markers, so the six steps have no hierarchy.
findings.reference: The competitor's step modules (01–03 and the six-step band) set each step with a large blue numeral and a bold title above lighter body text, divided by hairlines.
findings.fix: In reference.css style .process-step titles of the m8 list variant as bold (600–700) and one step above the body size, and replace the list markers with the .process-step__marker numerals in the accent blue.

findings.issue: splitMedia-3 is tinted and follows the tinted m4/m4-2 card set, so two neighbouring plain sections share the beige background (the same at 390 px).
findings.reference: The competitor alternates its sections between white, beige and navy, so neighbouring sections differ.
findings.fix: Have the template's tint alternation count splitMedia-3 after the m4 set so that it renders white (on --section-tint).

findings.issue: The navy step band has no heading in the page at all (no heading in the markup), so after the FAQ it reads as five loose figures with a button.
findings.reference: The competitor's navy step band opens with an eyebrow and an h2 ('HOW IT WORKS' / 'Six steps from Costing to delivery') over its columns.
findings.fix: Give the faq-steps block a section heading (for example a timeline title) in the page copy.

findings.issue: The button touches the last step's text with almost no gap (also at desktop), and each step numeral is set about 15 px in from the left edge the step titles start on.
findings.reference: The competitor's step numbers line up with their titles on one left edge, and its band buttons stand clear of the text above them.
findings.fix: In reference.css add a top margin (about 24–32 px) to the button in .process[data-variant=band], and remove the inline padding of .process-step__marker so the numeral starts on the title's edge.

findings.issue: On phones the wide hero photo is cropped to the centre, so the H1 sits over the subject's face, and the copy stops near the middle, leaving about 150 px of darkened photo with nothing on it below the button.
findings.reference: The competitor shows a portrait photo on phones, with the subject's face above and the title, lead and buttons set in the lower half.
findings.fix: Turn on the phoneHeroes variant in template-variants.json so phones get the portrait twin, and anchor the hero copy to the lower part of the frame.

findings.issue: The whole hero lead is set at weight 700, as heavy as the H1, so the four-line lead competes with the title.
findings.reference: The competitor's hero lead is regular weight with only key phrases in bold.
findings.fix: In reference.css set the hero lead (.hero p) to font-weight 400–500.

findings.issue: This split row has no heading: it opens on a lead paragraph and a table, so on its own background it reads as a stray table hanging off the m4 cards.
findings.reference: Each of the competitor's split rows ('Sustainable Swimwear Made In Bali', 'Planning your collection') opens with its own heading.
findings.fix: Give splitMedia-3 a section heading in the copy (for example on the sales and marketing strategy).

findings.issue: The empty top-left cell of the table carries a white scroll-fade smear on the beige panel; the same fade shows at the edges at 390 px.
findings.reference: The competitor's panels show no fades or gradients.
findings.fix: In reference.css make the table's scroll-edge fade use the panel's background (var(--surface-secondary)) or drop it when the table fits.

findings.issue: The three quote cards end about 100 px short of the content's right edge, so the row is ragged against the full-width sections above and below it.
findings.reference: The competitor's testimonial slider fills the content width with three equal slides in view.
findings.fix: In reference.css let the testimonials carousel track's slides fill the container when every slide shows (slide width = (100% − gaps) / 3).

findings.issue: The outlined button 'TALK TO US ABOUT CONSULTING' breaks onto two cramped lines inside its pill, unlike the same label in the hero, which keeps to one line.
findings.reference: The competitor's pill buttons on phones keep their label on one line.
findings.fix: In reference.css reduce the cta button's side padding and letter-spacing on phones (or let it span the column width) so the label fits on one line.

findings.issue: In the footer's brand column the STRANDMILL logo is left-aligned, but the contact lines and links under it are centred, so the column has two alignments (also at 390 px).
findings.reference: The competitor's 'STAY CONNECTED' column is centred as a whole: its heading, icons and links share one axis.
findings.fix: In reference.css give the footer brand column one alignment: either left-align the contact lines and links to the logo, or centre the logo with them.

findings.issue: The hero photo (general-hero-1) has its own headline 'Swim for Sunlit Days', a subline and two buttons ('Shop Swimwear', 'Explore the Collection') printed into the image, and they show through faintly behind our H1, lead and button, so the hero reads as two layers of overlapping text and dead buttons.
findings.reference: The competitor's hero photo is a clean shot with no lettering; its only text is the live title, lead and two buttons set over it.
findings.fix: Replace the /custom-swimwear-printing/ hero photo (media.heroByRoute in template-variants.json → general-hero-1) with a photo that has no lettering, and take general-hero-1 out of the general pool (it is used on other routes too) until it has been regenerated without the text.

findings.issue: The six steps use the browser's default '1.'–'6.' list numbers in body size and colour, and each step title ('Scale and trial print', 'A4 approval options'…) is the same weight as its description and barely larger, so the section reads as a plain ordered text list, not a process.
findings.reference: The competitor's '3 Ways to Handover' list marks each step with a large accent-blue '01'–'03' numeral in its own column, a bold title above the text and a thin rule between steps.
findings.fix: In reference.css for .block--process[data-variant="list"]: list-style none on .point-list__items with a counter rendered by ::before as decimal-leading-zero in var(--accent-text), weight 700, in its own grid column; .point-list__title font-weight 700 with a small margin under it; a 1px var(--border-color) top rule on each .point-list__item.

findings.issue: The seven-step list has the same bare rendering as m7: plain '1.'–'7.' numbers, and step titles ('Consultation and design', 'Tech pack and patterns'…) no bolder than their descriptions. Its only caption sits alone at body size in an otherwise empty left half.
findings.reference: The competitor's numbered steps have blue '01'–'03' numerals and heading-weight step titles.
findings.fix: Gets the same .block--process[data-variant="list"] numeral and title rules as m7 in reference.css. That one change styles both blocks.

findings.issue: Card titles are broken by hyphenation: 'Recycled subli-mation microfibre' in m2 and 'Base fab-ric requirements' in m2-2. Phones show the same break in 'Recycled subli-mation microfibre'.
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles ('Planning your collection', 'What sells and what doesnt') wrap between whole words.
findings.fix: Set hyphens: manual (and overflow-wrap: normal) on .feature-card__title in reference.css so titles wrap only between words.

findings.issue: Two sections of the same shape stand one under the other: m7 'Mock-ups, Strike-offs and Sample Approval' and m8 'Print Lead Times, Pricing and Order Terms' both set their rows of short items as a list beside their heading, so the same arrangement repeats.
findings.reference: Site rule: of two neighbouring sections made of short-item rows, the template sets only one as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: When a process list and an iconList are neighbours, have the template give m8 the other iconList arrangement (items under the heading in columns).

findings.issue: The list item titles ('Lower-cost repeat printing', 'Bulk production timing'…) are set in a light regular weight at almost the section heading's size with loose leading, and break as 'Lower-cost / repeat printing', so they read as loose large text rather than item titles. m3 and m5 show the same, and desktop shows the same weight.
findings.reference: The competitor's item and card titles are bold (Maison 700) and clearly smaller than the section heading.
findings.fix: Set font-weight: 700 and line-height: 1.3 on the iconList item title (.block--icon-list) in reference.css; the template keeps setting its size.

findings.issue: The check marks before each list item are pale aqua on the beige tint (m3, m5) and on white (m8), at roughly 1.5:1 contrast, so they barely show at either width.
findings.reference: The competitor's icons and markers are navy or steel blue on light backgrounds; non-text graphics need at least 3:1.
findings.fix: Set the checks marker colour (its color/stroke in .block--icon-list[data-variant="checks"]) to the dark accent var(--accent-text) in reference.css.

findings.issue: On phones an empty band of about 60px separates the heading 'Mock-ups, Strike-offs and Sample Approval' from step 1, much larger than the gaps between steps, so the list looks detached. splitMedia-1-steps has the same gap under its caption.
findings.reference: The competitor's step lists follow their heading at the normal heading-to-content gap.
findings.fix: In reference.css at the stacked breakpoint, reduce the row-gap between the intro column and .point-list__items in .block--process to the heading-to-content gap (about 1–1.5rem).

findings.issue: The fabric cards in m2, m2-2 and m10 are drawn with a dark near-black 1px outline on white or beige, so the grids read as boxed forms.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards ('Planning your collection', 'Plain colours' / 'Prints') are filled panels with no border: white on beige, or navy and aqua fills.
findings.fix: Switch the site-wide featureGrid variant to 'plain' in template-variants.json, or in reference.css drop the outlined card border to a light var(--border-color) hairline and lean on --surface-secondary for the panel.

findings.issue: The three testimonial cards keep a fixed width and stop at about 1350px of the 1440px page, so an empty strip about 200px wide is left at the right edge of the row with no controls to explain it.
findings.reference: The competitor's card rows fill their container edge to edge.
findings.fix: In reference.css, let the testimonial cards share the row when all of them fit (grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(18rem, 1fr)), or flex: 1 1 0 on .testimonial in the desktop track).

findings.issue: The testimonials band is painted mint (--surface-band-mint), a third background found nowhere else on the page and set for this one section type, not the page's white/beige tint.
findings.reference: The competitor uses only its beige tint and navy for section backgrounds; site rule: the treatment colours the tint through --section-tint, never one section.
findings.fix: Remove the background on .block--testimonials in reference.css (line 285) so the band takes the template's alternating --section-tint.

findings.issue: On phones the comparison table cuts its fourth column ('Pigment with white underlayer') off at the right edge, hinted only by a faint edge shadow, while the narrow first column breaks 'White or pastel areas' into one word per line.
findings.reference: The competitor shows its comparisons on phones as stacked panels (the 'Plain colours' / 'Prints' cards) with nothing cut off sideways.
findings.fix: Give the prose comparison chart (.prose__chart[data-chart="comparison"]) a stacked phone layout: one card per column with its rows as label/value pairs, like the table 'cards' variant, instead of the sideways scroll.

findings.issue: Every cell of the comparison table is ruled in a dark 1px line inside a white panel, so the small three-row table is dominated by its grid.
findings.reference: The competitor does not use ruled grids; its comparisons are separated by space and light panels.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set the cell border of .prose__table th and td to a light var(--border-color) horizontal rule only (no vertical lines).

findings.issue: The button label 'TALK TO US ABOUT CUSTOM PRINTING' wraps to two lines inside its outlined pill, so the pill turns into a tall lozenge with cramped text.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone buttons ('SEND US YOUR DESIGNS', 'TALK IT THROUGH FIRST') hold one line inside a full-width pill.
findings.fix: On phones in reference.css, make .block--cta .button full width (inline-size: 100%) with reduced letter-spacing and inline padding, so the label holds one line.

findings.issue: On phones the wide-variant photo keeps its desktop strip ratio (about 2.3:1) and shrinks to a 150px-high band under a long run of text, so the factory shot is too small to read.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone photos in text sections (the handover/mock-up image) run the full width at a near-square or 4:3 ratio.
findings.fix: In reference.css at the stacked breakpoint, give .block--split[data-variant="wide"] media an aspect-ratio of 4 / 3 (object-fit: cover).

findings.issue: In the brand column the STRANDMILL wordmark is left-aligned while the email, phone, address, hours and links under it are centred, so the column has two alignments. Phones show the same.
findings.reference: The competitor's footer brand column (STAY CONNECTED, icons, links) is centred as a whole.
findings.fix: Add text-align: center (or align-self: center) to the wordmark in .site-footer__brand in reference.css.
